findings.evidence: At the exact release, #[tool_handler] generates ServerHandler::call_tool only when the impl does not define call_tool. The generated body creates ToolCallContext::new(self, request, context) and awaits the configured ToolRouter.call. Therefore omitting a bespoke call_tool override is a concrete router-first seam, not only a model-level proposal.

ToolCallContext carries RequestContext, tool name, arguments, InputResponses and requestState. Standard FromContextPart implementations extract RequestContext, Parameters

, RequestState and InputResponses before invoking the registered handler body; malformed Parameters fail with invalid_params before handler materialization.

IntoCallToolResult directly supports InputRequiredResult and CallToolResponse. The exact-release upstream MacroMrtrServer test registers a tool taking Parameters + RequestState + InputResponses, returns Result<CallToolResponse, ErrorData>, emits InputRequired on round one and completes on retry through a real client/server pair.

CallToolResponse itself implements IntoCallToolResult, and Task is a CallToolResponse variant. Therefore a registered tool handler can return the Task variant by the exact source type path. The pinned upstream task E2E test still uses a manual ServerHandler::call_tool override, so registered-handler Task materialization was not independently runtime-tested in this worker.

#[tool_handler] only auto-generates get_info when the impl does not already define it. A safer refactor can therefore omit call_tool so the macro generates router-first dispatch while retaining a custom get_info that explicitly enables both tools and Tasks. The macro's autogenerated get_info alone enables tools/prompts but not Tasks.

The exact upstream AlwaysTaskServer deliberately calls TaskManager.spawn inside call_tool without checking client Tasks capability, then returns CallToolResponse::Task. The dispatch_rejects_task_result_for_non_declaring_client E2E test confirms framework dispatch rejects that response with MISSING_REQUIRED_CLIENT_CAPABILITY. Because spawn occurs before call_tool returns, the generic guard is a wire/response safeguard, not a pre-materialization fence.

The exact upstream TaskServer checks context.client_capabilities().supports_tasks() before spawning; a non-Tasks client follows the synchronous ToolRouter fallback, and the no_task_without_extension_capability E2E test verifies the synchronous result. Pre-spawn capability checking therefore belongs inside the task-capable implementation, not solely in post-handler dispatch.

The local execution environment reports `cargo: command not found`, so the source-qualified router-first task candidate could not be compiled or run against rmcp-v3.1.4 in this worker. No local compile success is claimed.

The bundled TaskManager remains in-memory/fresh-ID oriented for the examined path. Router-first policy parity does not solve persistent create-or-get, lost-CreateTaskResult recovery, process-restart redrive, or external-effect duplicate safety.
